newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares edge down at noon in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares edge down at noon in dull trade.

text.p: Shanghai B shares edged down in dull trade on Tuesday morning with most investors taking a wait-and-see attitude with market sentiment hurt by Monday's suspension of Shenzhen Development Bank, brokers said.
Hainan Airlines listing of 71 million B shares on Thursday on the Shanghai bourse is also attracting significant investor attention and pulling down trading volume, they said.
The B index fell 0.107 points or 0.13 percent to 85.374 points on very thin volume of 4.615 million shares worth $3.061 million.
"Yesterday's suspension of Shenzhen Development Bank showed the government's strong determination to curb the market, which made many investors more cautious," one broker said.

"Investors are more conservative and they would rather put more capital into new shares which in China have proved to be a safe investment," another broker said. "So most investors are holding money for the listing of Hainan Airlines."
Brokers said the market would not see a strong rebound ahead of the return of Hong Kong.

"The market will continue with the current low-key trading for the rest of this week," said a broker with a foreign brokerage in Shanghai. "If their are any signs of a new run of gains, it will be after the Hong Kong handover."
Of 44 B shares, 35 traded, with 11 down, eight flat and 16 up.
Wing Sung was the biggest loser on speculative selling, falling $0.010 or 3.99 percent to $0.240 on volume of 5,000 shares.
Jinan Qingqi Motorcycle 900946.SS was the most actively traded on profit-taking, ending the morning unchanged at $0.538 on volume 1.0 million shares.

Shanghai's A share index was slightly up on institutional support in selective stocks, but market sentiment is cautious after suspension of Shenzhen Development Bank on Monday afternoon, brokers said.
They said investor confidence that the government would not crack down on the market in the week ahead of the handover of Hong Kong had been smashed.
The index gained 9.387 points or 0.70 percent to 1,350.071 points on volume of 159.9 million shares worth 2.4 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index rose 32.937 points or 0.81 percent to 4,115.657 points.
Xinjiang Tebian was the star on institutional buying, jumping 0.77 yuan or 7.06 percent to 11.67 yuan on volume of 3.4 million shares.
